inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average DILUTED shares, Q2 2026 (10-Q filed 2026-08-07, us-gaap:WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding = 89.0M; cover page 89,098,299 at 2026-07-31). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge. Buybacks (FY2025 $153M, H1-2026 $58.8M) are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and are value-neutral here.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement: share-based compensation add-back $45.2M plus $23.6M cash taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards (financing section). PCA publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC line, so the two lines are summed. Interest income is left in the flows (not stripped) because PCA is a net-DEBT company (gross cash $443M vs $3.97B debt), so no cash pile is being double-counted.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-01T20:03:16Z regular close (NYSE, 1 Oct 2026); not an after-hours print
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in USD, the currency of the flows. Rf ~4.1% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.9 -> cost of equity ~8.6%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% on the post-Greif IG notes, ~3.8% after 25% tax. Market weights E ~84% / D ~16% (market cap ~$20.4B vs $3.97B debt) -> WACC ~7.8%, rounded to 8.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality and the pricing-durability risk are charged ONCE, in the scenario flows and weights, not again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating-lease cost is inside cost of sales/SG&A and therefore already deducted from EBITDA; operating-lease liabilities ($390.4M at 2025-12-31) are EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases are immaterial. One treatment (lease as operating cost), applied consistently; no lease_cost_pct_path needed.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, cyclical: industrials' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). PCA is a vertically integrated containerboard/corrugated producer; the flow is genuine free cash flow, net debt is real debt, so the default engine applies. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY entry). FY0 = FY2025 actuals (XBRL-derived Metrics.csv); Y1 = FY2026, which is ~75% elapsed at the valuation date and is still discounted a full period (conservative by well under 1% of EV). ANCHORS: price from Yahoo at price_as_of; net debt and diluted shares from the Q2-2026 10-Q (2026-06-30). GREIF: the $1.8B Greif containerboard business closed Sept-2025 and is funded by debt, which is why total debt stepped from ~$2.5B to ~$3.97B. In an unlevered DCF the capital-structure change shows up in net debt and in the WACC weights, not in EBITDA; what it DOES do to the flows is (i) add ~8-9pp to FY2026 revenue growth as the ~800kt of mill capacity and eight plants annualise, (ii) lift D&A to ~8% of revenue via purchase-accounting step-ups (H1-2026 D&A 401.5 on 4,857.6 revenue), (iii) dilute the pre-synergy margin slightly, offset by the >$30M guided synergy run-rate. CAGR/MARGIN ANCHORS: the CSV EBITDA is GAAP EBIT + D&A, i.e. POST-SBC; the engine's ebitda_margin_path is pre-SBC, so the FY2025 anchor is (1,759.8 + 45.2)/8,989.3 = 20.1%, and H1-2026 was also 20.1%. The FY2022 post-SBC peak was 22.1%, the FY2020 trough 17.0%, the FY2023-25 average 19.8%. Mid-cycle pre-SBC margin is set at 21.0% in the base (a little above the trailing three-year average because ~10% of US containerboard capacity has been permanently closed and Greif synergies accrue) - deliberately NOT the 2026-27 price-spike level. CASH TAX: FY2025 cash tax paid was $174M on ~$1.0B pre-tax (17%), depressed by restored 100% bonus depreciation on the ~$830M capex year; ramps 22% -> 25% statutory-plus-state by Y4. WORKING CAPITAL: manufacturer with receivables + inventory (~$2.2B) well above payables (~$0.6B), so growth consumes cash; wc_capture is NEGATIVE (-15% of the revenue change). DIVIDEND: $5.00/share (~$445M/yr) is a distribution of the FCF, not an additional charge. TERMINAL: 15x cap on Y10 owner FCF (top of the 12-15x cyclical range, reflecting PCA's best-in-class cost position); the cap binds in the base and bull, where Gordon at 8%/2-2.5% would be 17-18x.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR (12.1%) diverges >30% from equity 5yr CAGR (7.2%) and revenue 5yr CAGR (6.2%): FY2020 was a COVID/price-trough base year (EPS $4.86), so the EPS CAGR measures cycle recovery, not trend. The 3yr EPS CAGR is -8.1% off the FY2022 peak for the same reason. Neither is a forward growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs on FY2020->FY2025 (5yr) and FY2022->FY2025 (3yr). FCF CAGRs use the OWNER-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes; interest income not stripped because net debt): FY2020 571.1, FY2022 619.8, FY2025 659.8. Owner-FCF CAGR (2.9%/5yr) is below reported-FCF CAGR (3.6%/5yr) because SBC + equity-award taxes grew ~11%/yr (40.5 -> 68.8) against FCF at ~3.6%/yr: a rising share of reported FCF growth is being paid in stock. The forward base path is anchored to the Greif annualisation, the 2026 price increases and management guidance, not to these CAGRs; selected_growth_rate is retained as the PEG proxy only.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +11.5%: H1-2026 was +12.6% YoY on Greif annualisation plus the $70 (Mar) and $50 (Jun) per-ton increases; H2 adds the $140/ton Sept-1 increase with the Greif comp lapping only in Q4. FY2027 +5.5% is mostly the carry-over of the 2026 increases into a full year (~$126/ton incremental x ~5.5Mt at ~75% box realisation) with box volumes ~+1%. Thereafter 2.5-3% (volume ~1% + price ~1.5-2%) fading to 2% terminal.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC anchor 20.1% (FY2025 and H1-2026). FY2026 21.5% = H1 actual 20.1% and H2 ~22.8% implied by the raised Q3 guidance ($2.91 adj EPS vs $2.16 GAAP in Q2) net of the Riverville outage. FY2027 23.5% is the full-year of the $260/ton with some cost inflation and partial erosion, ABOVE the FY2022 peak (22.1% post-SBC = ~22.6% pre-SBC) because ~10% of US capacity has been permanently closed. Then the industry gives roughly half of the spike back over 2028-2031 to a 21.0% mid-cycle (~20.2% post-SBC vs the FY2023-25 average 19.8%, the difference being Greif synergies and a structurally tighter market).
base.capex_da_rationale: FY2026 capex ~8% (~$800M, in line with the FY2025 $829M and H1-2026 $371M run-rate incl. Greif mill work); D&A 8.0% in FY2026 (H1-2026 actual 8.3%) fading to 7.0% as the Greif step-up amortises and revenue grows; capex settles at 7.2%, a little above D&A, which is what a containerboard system needs to hold its cost position.

bull.rationale: The full $260/ton sticks through 2027-28 with no capacity restarts, Greif synergies exceed the >$30M guide, and the structurally tighter industry holds a 23% pre-SBC mid-cycle margin (~FY2022 peak made permanent). Reinvestment runs a little higher (8.5% capex in 2027) to debottleneck the acquired mills. Terminal growth 2.5% on e-commerce/reshoring volume.

bear.rationale: A normal containerboard cycle turn, not a tail: the $140/ton September increase is only partly recognised and rolls back in 2027 as idled capacity restarts and box demand softens; 2028 is a 2023-style down year (revenue -4%, pre-SBC margin 17.5% ~ the FY2020 trough) before a slow recovery to a 19.5% mid-cycle (~18.7% post-SBC, below the FY2023-25 average because the Paper segment keeps shrinking). Management cuts capex to ~6.5% in the trough, as it did in 2023, which cushions FCF. FY2026 can only fall so far because H1 is already booked at +12.6%.

scenario_narratives.base: PCA annualises the Greif containerboard business and realises most of the 2026 price increases ($70 Mar, $50 Jun, $140 Sep) over FY2026-27, lifting the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to ~23.5% in FY2027 - above the FY2022 peak because ~10% of US capacity has been permanently closed. Containerboard remains a capacity-utilisation commodity, so roughly half of that spike erodes over 2028-2031 to a 21% mid-cycle margin that is still a point above the FY2023-25 average, funded by Greif synergies (>$30M run-rate) and PCA's best-in-class mill cost position. Revenue growth settles at 2-2.5% (box volumes ~1% + modest price), capex runs a little above D&A at ~7.2% of revenue, cash tax normalises from the bonus-depreciation-depressed 17% to 25%, and growth consumes working capital. Net debt of ~$3.5B from the debt-funded deal is deducted at the Q2-2026 balance sheet.
scenario_narratives.bull: The industry's capacity discipline holds: no restarts, the full $260/ton sticks, and PCA's integrated system converts it at best-in-class margins, so pre-SBC EBITDA margin sits at 25% in 2027-28 and the mid-cycle resets to 23% (the FY2022 peak made structural). Greif synergies run well past the $30M guide and the acquired mills are debottlenecked with a modestly higher capex year. E-commerce and reshoring keep box volumes growing ~1-2%, supporting 2.5% terminal growth. Even here the terminal value is capped at 15x owner FCF - the bull case is about the level of cash flow, not a richer exit multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: The September $140/ton increase proves to be the top of the cycle: it is only partly recognised, idled competitor capacity restarts into 2027, and an industrial/consumer slowdown cuts box shipments, producing a 2023-style down year in 2028 (revenue -4%, margin at the FY2020 trough). The doubled debt load (~$3.5B net) is serviceable (ND/EBITDA stays under ~2x) but removes the balance-sheet optionality PCA historically had, and the Paper segment's secular decline drags the mid-cycle margin to ~19.5% pre-SBC. Capex is cut in the trough as in 2023, so FCF does not collapse, but the recovery is slow and terminal growth is 1.5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear UP to 25%: the valuation is being made at a cycle high - an 'unprecedented' $140/ton increase on top of $120/ton earlier in the year, with ~10% of US capacity just closed - and containerboard has historically given such spikes back; a normal cycle turn is a 1-in-4 outcome over the next three years, not a tail. Bull DOWN to 25%: it requires two independent things to hold simultaneously (the full price increase sticking AND no capacity restarts) plus synergies beating guidance. Base 50%: the Greif annualisation and the H1-2026 run-rate are already booked, so the centre of the distribution is well anchored.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF of a best-in-class but cyclical containerboard producer, valued at a mid-cycle margin rather than the FY2026-27 price-spike margin, with the Greif acquisition's debt deducted at the latest balance sheet and its capacity and synergies in the flows. SBC plus equity-award taxes are expensed and the diluted share count held flat; working capital consumes cash with growth; cash tax ramps to statutory; the terminal value is capped at 15x Y10 owner FCF so a small change in terminal growth cannot swing the answer. Risk is charged once - in the scenario flows and weights - not again in the WACC. The market is paying roughly 30x trailing earnings for PCA; the required-return table says what IRR that price implies on the base path, and the band between house and street values shows how little of the gap is SBC accounting (SBC is <1% of revenue).
key_risks_to_valuation: Containerboard price durability: the base assumes roughly half of the 2026 $260/ton is given back by 2031; if the industry's post-closure discipline holds, value sits between base and bull, if it collapses as in 2023 the bear path applies
Mid-cycle margin level: each 1pp of terminal pre-SBC EBITDA margin is ~$9-10/share at a 15x cap
Capex intensity: PCA has run capex at 8-9.7% of revenue in 2022 and 2025; if the mill-modernisation cadence stays at that level rather than the 7.2% assumed, FCF conversion is ~10% lower
Terminal multiple: the 15x owner-FCF cap is below the ~30x the market currently pays; the valuation embeds multiple compression, which is a stance, not a forecast
Greif integration and leverage: synergies are ahead of plan per management, but a trough with ~$3.5B net debt would constrain buybacks and capex timing
Secular decline of the Paper segment (~8% of revenue) is a permanent drag on the consolidated growth rate
